coverage_notes:
SOURCES USED. The backbone of this list is Auburn's own in-season staff directory: the "2010 Auburn Football Roster" page on auburntigers.cstv.com, Wayback-captured Sept. 9, 2010 (mid-2010 season), whose "Coaches" block lists 21 people spanning on-field coaches, football operations, strength, chaplain and medical staff. That is supplemented by (a) the archived Auburn Football Strength and Conditioning Staff page, (b) individual archived AuburnTigers.com staff bio pages, (c) the archived BCS National Championship Game notes PDF (Jan. 10, 2011), and (d) Wikipedia.

CONTINUITY / RING RULE. No mid-season arrivals or departures are documented. The BCS championship game notes explicitly state Auburn returned its entire coaching staff from the prior season and no in-season staff change surfaced in any source, so all 26 people below are treated as on staff at the Jan. 10, 2011 title game. The BCS game notes independently confirm all nine on-field assistants were with the team at the championship game itself (the "ASSISTANTS IN BOWLS" table), which is the strongest possible evidence for the ring rule for those nine plus Chizik.

CAVEAT ON THE STRENGTH STAFF. Ryan Russell, T.J. Graham and Jesse Kelley are documented from a Mar. 12, 2011 capture of the strength-staff page (two months AFTER the title game) because no in-season 2010 capture of that page exists in the Wayback Machine — captures jump from Mar. 2009 to Mar. 2011. Their 2010-season presence is nonetheless well supported by their own archived bios, which give "Joined Auburn Staff: January 2010" (Russell), "Joined AU Staff: June 2010" (Graham) and "Joined Auburn Staff: January 2009" (Kelley) — all before the 2010 season. I have flagged the capture date in each source note rather than asserting an in-season snapshot I do not have.

WHAT I COULD NOT DOCUMENT — this list is very likely INCOMPLETE. (1) The 2010 Auburn football media guide, which would have carried the full support-staff directory, was published only as an Issuu embed (issuu.com/mjefferis/docs/auburn_football_2010_media_guide.opt); that document now returns 404, Issuu blocks direct reader-API access, and no PDF copy exists in the Wayback Machine. (2) Auburn's own "Football Support Staff" page (aub-support-staff.html) has no Wayback capture between Apr. 17, 2009 and 2012, so the site's dedicated support-staff directory for 2010 is unrecoverable; I deliberately did not use the 2009 capture, since that predates the championship season. (3) The 2010-11 bowl guide PDF is referenced by an archived wrapper page but the PDF itself was never captured. As a result I have NO equipment staff, NO academic-services staff, NO recruiting/administrative assistants, and almost certainly an incomplete set of graduate assistants and quality-control coaches. Auburn in this era would typically have carried roughly four graduate assistants; I could document only one (Rhett Lashlee, offensive GA) plus one quality-control coach (Casey Woods). Auburn's own Sept. 2010 "Coaches" listing simply omitted GAs and QC staff, which is why those two had to be sourced separately.

CASEY WOODS is the one row whose only sourcing is Wikipedia — the 2010 team-season page ("Quality Control: Casey Woods") corroborated by his own biography page, whose infobox shows "2009–2011" / "Auburn (OQC)" (offensive quality control). His AuburnTigers.com staff bio was never archived. I judged two independent Wikipedia pages sufficient to include him rather than drop a real, well-attested staffer, but it is weaker evidence than the rest of the list.

RESEARCH LIMITATION. This session's web-search budget was already exhausted before I began, so I could not search contemporary news coverage (hire announcements, championship-coverage features) — step 4 of the requested source ladder went unexecuted. All findings come from Wikipedia, Wayback Machine CDX/archived pages, and the archived championship game-notes PDF. A run with search available would likely recover several more GAs, quality-control coaches and equipment/academic staff.

NO NAMES WERE ADDED WITHOUT A SOURCE. Every row carries at least one verbatim quote checked programmatically against the whitespace-normalized text of the fetched page or extracted PDF.
